options: Flips the target qubit if and only if the control qubit is |1⟩; otherwise leaves the target alone
Flips both qubits regardless of their states
Flips the control qubit if and only if the target qubit is |1⟩
Measures the control qubit and discards the target
questions.explain: CNOT reads the control qubit without changing it, and applies X to the target only when that control is |1⟩.

questions.q: In the |00⟩, |01⟩, |10⟩, |11⟩ basis, what does CNOT (control=q1, target=q2) do to |10⟩?
options: Maps it to |11⟩
Maps it to |01⟩
Leaves it as |10⟩
Maps it to |00⟩
questions.explain: The control bit is 1, so the target flips from 0 to 1, turning |10⟩ into |11⟩ — confirmed by the matrix-vector computation in the lesson.

questions.q: Why is CNOT its own inverse (CNOT² = I)?
options: Flipping the target conditionally and then flipping it conditionally again under the identical condition undoes the first flip
Because CNOT has no effect on any input state
Because the control qubit is always measured between the two applications
Because X and CNOT are the same gate
questions.explain: The condition (control = |1⟩) doesn't change between the two applications, so the second CNOT exactly reverses whatever flip the first one made.

questions.q: How does CNOT differ from applying X independently to both qubits (X⊗X)?
options: X⊗X flips both qubits unconditionally on every input, while CNOT only flips the target and only when the control is |1⟩
They are mathematically identical gates
X⊗X only works on the control qubit
CNOT flips both qubits unconditionally, same as X⊗X
questions.explain: On |10⟩, X⊗X gives |01⟩, while CNOT gives |11⟩ — different outputs on the same input, because CNOT's flip is conditional and X⊗X's is not.

questions.q: Does CNOT applied to a basis state (like |10⟩) create entanglement?
options: No — the output is still a single basis state, which is always separable
Yes — every application of CNOT produces an entangled state
Only if the target qubit was already in superposition
Yes, but only when the control qubit is |0⟩
questions.explain: CNOT maps basis states to basis states; a single basis state is always a product state with no entanglement. Entanglement requires acting on a superposition across the control qubit first.
